newsitem.title: Philippines: Tropical storm not a threat to Philippine coconuts.
newsitem.headline: Tropical storm not a threat to Philippine coconuts.

text.p: Tropical Storm Peter threatening the northeastern Philippines will not affect the coconut industry as most of the country's biggest farms were not in its path, traders said on Tuesday.

"Yes, there is a storm coming, but I think it will bring us more rains than winds, and I think it won't damage any crop because the direction of the storm is going north," a coconut oils trader at a major commodities house in Manila said.
Market conditions too were fairly quiet with buyers as well as sellers on the sidelines, he said.
The bulk of Philippine cocnut production is from the southern island of Mindanao.
Forecaster Weather Services Corp said on Tuesday Storm Peter, with 40 mph winds, was near 13.7n/128.2e, moving west at five mph.
It was expected to intensify slowly and turn more northwest with time, taking the storm to the east of Luzon island.
Luzon is the northern group of islands in the Philippines, the world's largest producer of coconuts.
"Within Luzon, coconuts are only grown in southern Luzon," the trader said.
Local forecaster, the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA), said the storm may hit central and northern Luzon provinces starting on Wednesday.
